Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Alright welcome everyone, this is Alex from Redwood, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Alex, AE, Priya here is our Solutions Engineer, Jordan is your Customer Success lead. Who wants to kick off from Silver Oaks?
[00:12] Rachel Gomez: Hi all, Rachel here. We're excited to get the runtime onboarding started. We've been evaluating Redwood for a couple months, want to make sure the Dedicated lane meets our latency and security needs.
[00:22] Tom Patel: Tom, platform. We'll handle peering and infra, want to understand requirements and network flow.
[00:27] Lena Ortiz: Lena, security. I'll be validating SOC 2 controls, KMS integration, and data retention.
[00:32] Alex Chen: Great. Agenda — quick scoping of success criteria, review of the onboarding playbook, network and security checklist, then next steps. Priya will run through the runtime and pilot config.
[00:45] Priya Nair: Thank you. I'll start with the high-level runtime options. Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC options. For Silver Oaks you mentioned wanting data isolation plus low 99th percentile latency, so Dedicated or Private are the main fits.
[01:02] Rachel Gomez: Correct, we need to ensure sub-200ms p99 for the short prompts in prod. Cost is a secondary consideration but still important.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Sub-200ms p99 is doable depending on model and sequence length. For example, with our optimized LLM variants and continuous batching tuned to low concurrency, Dedicated pools on A100/RTX 8000 class can hit 100-180ms for 512 token sequences. There's variance with larger contexts and KV cache cold starts.
[01:34] Tom Patel: When you say KV cache cold starts, can you explain the warmup pattern? We want predictable performance when traffic spikes.
[01:41] Priya Nair: Sure. When a new model instance boots or a cache miss happens, the KV requires population which adds a few hundred ms for the first request. We mitigate with prefix caching, pre-warmed instances, and sticky routing. For Dedicated pilot we recommend a small burst pool with autoscale buffer to smooth spikes.
[02:00] Lena Ortiz: From security perspective, KMS integration is critical. We need to know what of our keys stay on customer side. Is the Private deployment the only option for customer-managed keys?
[02:09] Alex Chen: Good question. Private offers full KMS/HSM integration where customer-managed keys never leave your control plane. Dedicated can also integrate with customer KMS via a key-wrap mode, but there are architecture differences. We'll share a clear doc on KMS modes.
[02:24] Rachel Gomez: Also data residency — all logs and payloads for the pilot must remain in our EU region, please.
[02:30] Jordan Mills: Noted. We can pin region for Dedicated pools and Private nodes. We'll include region residency in the runbook.
[02:36] Priya Nair: I'm going to share my screen to go over the onboarding runbook link and the initial benchmark checklist. (link shared: https://redwood.example.com/runbook/socap-onboard)
[02:50] Alex Chen: Quick note — the runbook includes network CIDR, firewall rules, CDN edge hints, and a perf spreadsheet. We'll post a copy in the CRM.
[02:58] Tom Patel: Perfect. Can you call out the specific ports and IP ranges needed for VPC peering? We prefer not to open a wide range.
[03:06] Priya Nair: Yes, the required egress is TLS to our control plane on 443 and gRPC ports for the runtime (optional), we'll send the exact CIDR list. For Private we'll need peering and a small set of subnets for the inference nodes.
[03:20] Rachel Gomez: On the SLA, Silver Oaks requires 99.9% uptime for production with latency SLOs at p99 under 200ms. Is that something Redwood has offered for Dedicated customers?
[03:32] Alex Chen: We have SLA-backed tiers for Dedicated (SLA depends on contract). 99.9% uptime is within our enterprise plan. Latency SLOs are part of our runbooks and we include tracing hooks in the Console to monitor token-level latency.
[03:46] Lena Ortiz: For compliance proof, can you share audit logs and retention policies? We'll need to map to our internal controls.
[03:52] Jordan Mills: Absolutely — security pack link shared (https://redwood.example.com/security/socap-pack). It includes SOC 2 Type II report, ISO attestation, logging model, and sample audit logs.
[04:04] Lena Ortiz: Thanks. One quick transcription typo I saw in the doc earlier — 'KV cache' was sometimes written as 'KV cash' — small but confusing.
[04:11] Priya Nair: Good catch. We'll clean that up in the shared doc.
[04:14] Tom Patel: On the Dedicated pilot — what minimal commit do we need to prove performance? We want a two-week pilot that mirrors production burst patterns.
[04:23] Priya Nair: For a realistic test we recommend a 2-week Dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool sized to expected concurrency — typically 2-4 GPUs depending on model family. We'll instrument with our perf harness and share the benchmark sheet.
[04:36] Rachel Gomez: Can we run both quantized and full-fp runs? We need quality comparisons.
[04:41] Priya Nair: Yes — we can run q4/q5 quantized variants alongside fp16 runs. Our Optimize team will recommend quantization profiles per workload to balance cost and quality.
[04:52] Alex Chen: I'll have Priya send a proposed pilot config with GPUs, expected throughput, and a step-down plan if the quality delta is unacceptable.
[04:59] Tom Patel: Network question — do you support transit gateways or only VPC peering? We use TGW for cross-account routing.
[05:07] Priya Nair: We support both; for Private deployments TGW works as long as the routing is propagated. For Dedicated, we usually do VPC peering but TGW is supported with some route tables adjustments. We'll document exact routing.
[05:20] Lena Ortiz: Encryption-in-transit and at-rest — confirm both and whether logs are salted or pseudonymized by default?
[05:27] Jordan Mills: All in-transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. At-rest encryption is handled by cloud provider keys by default; for Private/Dedicated you can provide KMS. Logs by default are retained for 30 days and can be redacted; we can set longer retention or send to your SIEM via secure pipeline.
[05:48] Rachel Gomez: That sounds good. For access control we need SSO/SAML and RBAC mapped to our teams. Does Redwood support SCIM for provisioning?
[05:56] Alex Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported and we have SCIM-based provisioning for user sync. We'll include our SSO runbook and attribute mapping suggestions.
[06:06] Tom Patel: Regarding rollouts — can we do canary traffic splits between two model versions and automatic fallback if latency spikes?
[06:14] Priya Nair: Absolutely. Our Console supports canary rollouts and automated fallback policies. For Dedicated it's a config you control per-route. We also provide tracing hooks to correlate model versions to token-level latency and cost.
[06:28] Rachel Gomez: On cost — what's the expected cost difference between quantized Dedicated and Private on-prem? Just a high level.
[06:34] Priya Nair: Quantized Dedicated often reduces GPU memory and improves throughput so unit cost drops — typically 20–40% cheaper depending on model. Private on-prem avoids provider costs but increases ops overhead; overall TCO depends on utilization. We'll include a cost model spreadsheet in the benchmark artifact.
[06:52] Tom Patel: Great. Can we demo the Console and the trace view?
[06:57] Priya Nair: Yes, quick demo now. (screen: Console live) Here is the per-route latency waterfall, token-level cost, and the rollout control. Note the 'prefix cache hit rate' metric — that really impacts p95/p99.
[07:18] Rachel Gomez: Nice. On that trace waterfall, can we export traces to our Datadog?
[07:22] Priya Nair: Yes, we support exporting traces/metrics via OTLP and have a Datadog integration.
[07:28] Lena Ortiz: A couple of compliance items — we need encrypted audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance, and we need to see IAM role assumptions in the deployment.
[07:36] Jordan Mills: We'll include an architecture diagram and an example IAM role with least privilege in the runbook. Forwarding encrypted logs to Splunk is part of our observability add-on.
[07:48] Rachel Gomez: Anything else? We want to make sure the pilot covers routing policies, batching config, and a simulated production traffic mix.
[07:55] Priya Nair: We'll run the perf harness with your sample prompts and the production QPS profile. For batching we'll test continuous batching thresholds and observe latency tradeoffs.
[08:06] Tom Patel: Who will own the test harness? We have internal SREs who can run it but will need credentials and guidance.
[08:12] Alex Chen: Redwood can host the harness remotely and run benchmarks with you, or we can provide the harness scripts and you run them inside your infra. For initial pilot we usually run together to ensure parity.
[08:23] Rachel Gomez: Let's do joint runs.
[08:26] Alex Chen: Good. Now quick recap of next steps and owners. Priya will share runbook and bench checklist, Alex will send contract the pilot template, Tom will provide network details, Lena will give compliance checklist items. We'll schedule the VPC walkthrough.
[08:41] Jordan Mills: I'll create a calendar invite for the VPC/network session and add onboarding Jira tickets.
[08:48] Tom Patel: One more question — any recommended warmup script to avoid cold KV misses when we flip to prod?
[08:54] Priya Nair: We have a warmup script in the runbook that sequentially hits common prompt prefixes to populate KV cache. We'll include it in the runbook link.
[09:05] Rachel Gomez: Sounds great. Anything blocking on our end besides the network diagrams and compliance confirmation?
[09:12] Lena Ortiz: We'll review the security pack, likely a few questions but no major blockers.
[09:17] Alex Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts in an email and the CRM.
[09:23] Rachel Gomez: Thank you.
[09:26] Alex Chen: Meeting adjourned.
